c.tagline: The pilgrimage endpoint of the Camino de Santiago, crowned by a baroque cathedral holding the apostle's relics

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small pilgrim albergues and market stalls

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €3.90 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard and reliable

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

religion: Roman Catholic (majority, reinforced by the pilgrimage tradition)
walk: The old town is compact, pedestrianized, and very walkable; the cathedral square is the natural center of any visit

safety.safety: Very safe city, popular with solo pilgrims and travelers of all ages
safety.crime: Petty theft near the cathedral and train station is the main concern

hood_landmark.Casco Histórico (Old Town): Praza do Obradoiro and the Cathedral of Santiago
hood_landmark.Zona Nova (New Town / Ensanche): Rúa do Franco's shopping and dining strip
hood_landmark.San Lázaro: The Palacio de Congresos and modern convention district
hood_landmark.Zona Universitaria: University of Santiago de Compostela's historic campus buildings
hood_landmark.Fontiñas: Fontiñas' modern residential blocks and local markets

avoid.reason: Minor pickpocketing around the cathedral and Praza do Obradoiro during peak pilgrim months.

hood_desc: The granite-paved medieval core around the cathedral, packed with pilgrim albergues, tapas bars, and souvenir shops; the natural base for nearly every visitor.
The 19th-century commercial expansion just beyond the old walls, with wider streets, department stores, and everyday local life.
A modern district anchored by the convention center, mainly of interest for business travelers rather than sightseers.
The historic university quarter with grand academic buildings and a young, lively student atmosphere.
A residential, largely local neighborhood with little tourist infrastructure, useful mainly for longer stays or budget apartments.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Galicia.

transit.sys: Tranvías de Santiago urban bus network
transit.pay: Cash or contactless card on board; rechargeable travel card available
transit.note: The old town is pedestrian-only, so buses mainly serve outlying neighborhoods and the airport

transport.air: Santiago-Rosalía de Castro Airport (SCQ), about 20 min from the city
transport.train: Renfe high-speed and regional trains connect to A Coruña, Vigo, and Madrid
transport.bus: ALSA and Monbus coaches connect to Galician towns and the rest of Spain
transport.car: Well connected via the AP-9 motorway; not needed for the old town itself

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Movistar, Vodafone, or Orange tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for guides and tours
tip.r: 5-10% for good service, not expected at casual bars
